dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Exhaustive reading of types.rs/decode.rs/runtime.rs/spec.rs/main.rs, producing an explicit map: V128 already defined as [u8;16], exec_numeric stub (717-719), V128 lane helper stubs (728-754), 0xFC handled but 0xFD absent, validate_module stub, spec.rs already parses V128, public items frozen. Level-8-quality skeleton orientation.
Invented/guessed SIMD 0xFD sub-opcode numbers ('0x00 = v128.load... 0x0C = v128.const') rather than deriving them from spec or wabt — assumptions baked into hundreds of opcodes without verification.

Per-family semantics (signed vs unsigned lane extract, f32x4 comparison mask width) discovered reactively via test-output symptoms, not pinned down from the spec beforehand — guessing rather than research.

First and only use of wasm2wat to verify the 0xFD opcode mapping, occurring after submit attempts; root-cause of the 0.298 failure identified as 'incorrect SIMD opcode mapping (verified via wasm2wat)'. The right research act, performed far too late to be the sustained re-research of level 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's understanding of the provided skeleton is genuinely strong and explicit (level-8 territory): it read every source, catalogued which functions are stubbed vs buggy, located where value types/decoding/memory/execution are wired, and respected the frozen public contract. But the other half of this dimension — the SIMD binary encoding and lane semantics — was handled by guessing opcode numbers and reverse-engineering semantics from test failures, with wabt cross-checking only as a terminal gesture after the task had already failed. Pinning down non-obvious semantics from the spec (the level-8 clause) never happened proactively, so despite the excellent skeleton map the encoding-research gap holds it to a 6.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: From the outset states a consistent two-phase decomposition: fix MVP (exec_numeric) first, then add SIMD; repeated across many early steps.

Decomposes SIMD into dependency-ordered infrastructure layers (types/SimdOp -> decode 0xFD -> V128 lane helpers -> exec_simd -> validate_module), sequencing shared primitives like lane accessors before the arithmetic that depends on them.

Mentions implementing SIMD 'in groups: memory loads/stores, splat, lane extract/replace, bitwise, integer arith...', showing family-level grouping but as a plan for one coordinated pass rather than a per-family loop.
Uses specific spec_json files (simd_const, simd_lane, simd_i8x16_cmp) as checkpoints and reads per-family pass rates — spec-test-bound done-checks, though run after a bulk implementation.

Implements ALL remaining SIMD families (f32x4/f64x2, narrowing/widening, conversions, dot product, Q15, lane load/store) in a single undifferentiated push rather than family-by-family with individual exit checks — the coarseness that keeps this below the 8 anchor.
Late milestone state is tracked as a flat 'remaining issues' list and aggregate score, not an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with pass targets.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into dependency-ordered infrastructure (lane helpers/types/decode before arithmetic), binding checkpoints to specific spec_json files — clearly exceeding anchor 5. However it never maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 opcode families with per-family pass targets; instead it implements all arithmetic/float/conversion families in one big-bang push and verifies with loose aggregate/spot checks, falling short of anchor 8's disciplined milestone hierarchy. This places it at a 6, between the family-grouped checkpointing of 5 and the explicit dependency-aware milestone plan of 8.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: After implementing exec_numeric, ran i32.json and read exact pass count (2/459→376/459), correctly attributing the 83 remaining failures to assert_invalid + the validate_module stub — per-family verification with specific failure attribution.

Systematic loop: ran simd_const/lane/i8x16_cmp per-family, read panic-by-line diagnostics (runtime.rs:950 'range start index 28 out of range'), and identified semantic bugs (signed/unsigned lane extract wrong), fixing each before moving on.

Ran a spread of individual SIMD family jsons (const, i16x8_arith, splat, bitwise, boolean, f32x4/f64x2_cmp) and kept re-checking MVP i32.json to guard against regressions while monitoring the aggregate score.

Built its own aggregate runner and treated the score as a monitored signal (0.247→0.298), but the loop stalled — the same analysis/score repeated verbatim across many steps without tightening to green.

Late anchor-10 behavior: used wasm2wat to disassemble test binaries and verify 0xFD opcode mapping, distinguishing an encoding mismatch from execution bugs — but this root-cause verification arrived after multiple submits and was never resolved.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently built and ran per-family spec-test jsons after implementing each family, read specific FAIL reasons (pass counts, panic line numbers, sign/bounds semantics), and periodically ran a self-built aggregate runner while re-checking MVP files — matching the anchor-8 systematic loop with regression guarding. It also showed partial anchor-10 traits (sign/lane-bounds semantic diagnosis and a wasm2wat encoding-vs-bug distinction). However, those advanced diagnostics came very late and were never carried through, the per-family loop rarely reached green, and the aggregate score was more repeatedly lamented than actively recovered, so the behavior falls short of a sustained 8 and lands at 7.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Early systematic inventory of stubs (exec_numeric, V128 helpers, missing 0xFD decoder) and a bulleted 'we need to' list, establishing an accurate done/remaining picture of the surface.

Reconciled per-family pass counts against the aggregate: MVP 376/459, simd_const 434/445, lane 142/463, i8x16_cmp 413/443, f32x4_cmp 660/2605, f64x2_cmp 202/2683; built its own runner since /tests/run_tests.py was absent.
Explicitly caught a regression — aggregate dropped from 0.299 to 0.247 after changes — showing it monitors aggregate movement, not just local family status.
Repeated 'still need / still missing' ledgers naming each remaining SIMD family (float arith, narrowing, widening, conversions, dot, Q15, lane load/store), tracking coverage across the long horizon.

Long plateau at 0.298 with near-verbatim repeated status analyses and multiple premature 'complete' submissions; eventually detected stuckness and diagnosed root cause (wrong opcode mapping via wasm2wat), quantifying ~23,700 failing assertions — but late and with visible thrashing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate, continuously updated inventory of families and per-family pass counts, reconciled them against the aggregate score, and noticed a regression (0.299→0.247) and the highest-remaining-assertion families — squarely above anchor 5 and hitting several anchor-8 behaviors. It falls short of 8-10 because it lingered on a 0.298 plateau repeating identical status analyses and submitting 'complete' multiple times before it caught the stall and pivoted to root-cause opcode verification, so thrashing was detected late rather than early and effort was not crisply reallocated. This places it at a 7.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Genuine course-correction: after breaking compilation by changing everything at once, restored all files from backups and switched to an incremental apply-build-test approach — abandoning a falsified strategy.
Repeated backup restores to escape broken compile states, explicitly reasoning 'we need to get back to a clean MVP state, then add SIMD correctly' — a real process pivot.
Diagnostic pivot: considered disabling validate_module to isolate validation vs execution failures, then reasoned through the tradeoff before deciding.
Identified 'incorrect SIMD opcode mapping' as the generator of failures early and restated it repeatedly, but kept adding features / re-doing validate_module instead of fixing the named root cause.

Score frozen at 0.298 across many submit attempts; root cause (opcode mapping) only investigated at the very end (256-263) via wasm2wat, and abandoned when the tool didn't support SIMD — circular re-debugging without fixing the generator.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows some real adaptation — it recovered from a broken 'change everything' state by restoring backups and going incremental, and made a diagnostic pivot around validate_module — which lifts it above anchor 0/3. But its dominant behavior matches recognition-without-correction: it verbally named the shared opcode-mapping generator from step 154 onward yet barrelled ahead adding features for ~100 steps, leaving the score stuck at 0.298 and only half-heartedly probing the root cause at the very end. That falls short of anchor 5's 'reconsiders AND adjusts,' placing it at a 4.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
